candidate_claims.text: Heartiest greetings to all of you across the country who are connected with this celebration of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas.
The heroic stories of Raghuji Bhangare, Bhagoji Naik, and Veer Baburao Shedmake are connected to this land.
Friends, The observance of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, which began on 15 November 2021, has now become a national celebration.
Last year, on the 150th birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, more than two lakh programmes were organised across the country.

Friends, On the occasion of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas today, more than 170 projects related to tribal development have been inaugurated across different states of the country, and foundation stones have been laid for more than 70 projects.

In addition, among the projects being inaugurated and launched are educational institutions, healthcare facilities, marketing centres for tribal products, and numerous initiatives related to expanding basic amenities in villages.
Across different states of the country, projects worth nearly ₹3000 crore have been inaugurated or had their foundation stones laid.
The first achievement is that nearly 50 crore people have overcome extreme poverty and risen out of it.
Both these achievements are deeply connected with the lives of our tribal brothers and sisters.
A few weeks ago, the World Bank report stated that nearly 50 crore people in India have emerged from extreme poverty over the past 12–13 years.
This is a very large number, 50 crore people.
The decisions taken by the central government and the schemes launched for tribal welfare in recent years have also played a major role in this achievement.
It has created confidence that India can fulfil its resolutions and that every Indian can achieve great goals.
For the PM-JANMAN Scheme and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan, we allocated a budget of more than ₹1 lakh crore.
Our effort was that the families who received facilities the latest after Independence should now receive them the fastest.
We built more than four crore permanent houses for poor families across the country.
Electricity was provided to 18,000 villages where it had not reached even after so many decades of Independence.
Through the Ayushman Bharat scheme, free healthcare worth up to ₹5 lakh was provided.
More than 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs were established across the country, allowing healthcare benefits to reach even remote tribal areas.
When poor families received toilets and sanitation facilities improved, the risk of many diseases was also reduced.
Through the Mudra Yojana, we provided collateral-free loans.
Under this scheme, assistance worth lakhs of crores of rupees was provided.
